clue.text: Second dismissal not going as intended

blocks.note: to second a motion is to back it
firing is dismissal from a job

explanation.surface: A second sacking at work turns out badly for whoever ordered it.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan that backfires has the opposite effect to what was wanted, so it is failing to go to plan.

clue.text: Horse carrying bishop is little one

indicators.note: a horse carrying something holds it on its back, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: a bay is a reddish-brown horse
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A horse with a bishop on its back turns out to be a small foal.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby is an infant, a small child, which is what 'little one' means as an affectionate phrase.

clue.text: Either side of cooker with raised temperature? That's not good

indicators.note: either side means one end or the other, so the outermost letters are wanted, joined by the word 'or'

blocks.note: 'either side' read literally is first letter OR last letter: C, then OR, then R
raised means up
T is the standard abbreviation for temperature

explanation.surface: A cooker heating up on both sides is a worrying sign in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: The trick is taking 'either' as the word OR placed between the two end letters of cooker. The definition is the whole closing remark, read as an adjective meaning bad.
explanation.definitionFit: Corrupt means dishonest or morally rotten, so it describes something that is not good.

clue.text: Place for wounded men filled with pathos, I recollected

indicators.note: re-collected means gathered up again and put together afresh, so the letters are regathered in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A soldier remembers a battlefield ward, full of sadness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recollected' reads as 'remembered', but split as re-collected it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A field hospital is a temporary medical post set up near a battle to treat injured soldiers.

clue.text: Drawing instruments — dividers, perhaps

blocks.note: first meaning: straight-edged strips for drawing lines
second meaning: those who govern, as in 'divide and rule'

explanation.walkthrough: Dividers are also a drawing instrument, so the clue seems to list stationery; the second sense refers to governors who divide and rule.
explanation.definitionFit: Rulers are both measuring strips for lines and people who govern, some of whom keep power by dividing their subjects.

clue.text: No male in demonstration, as a rule

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it is placed inside it

blocks.note: taken as written
a rally is a mass demonstration
M is the standard abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: As usual, no men turn up at the protest.
explanation.definitionFit: Normally and 'as a rule' are both phrases meaning usually or in most cases.

clue.text: Good antique that's often bought as investment

definitions.note: a descriptive definition for a thing

blocks.note: G is the standard abbreviation for good
an antique thing is old

explanation.surface: A sound piece of antique is frequently purchased for its value as an investment.
explanation.definitionFit: Gold bullion and coins are a classic store of wealth that people buy to protect their savings.

clue.text: Top gear, in general

blocks.note: first meaning: a protective coat or smock worn over other clothes
second meaning: taken as a whole

explanation.walkthrough: 'Top gear' suggests the highest gear of a car (or the TV show); here it is clothing worn on top of other clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: An overall is a garment worn over clothes, and as an adverb overall means taking everything into account.

clue.text: Cutting up middle slice of dessert, in manner of speaking

indicators.note: a slice from the middle means only the central letters of the following word are kept
one thing being in another means it is placed inside it

blocks.note: diction is one's manner of speaking
the central three of its seven letters

explanation.surface: Someone slicing up a pudding, describing it in elaborate language.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle three letters of dessert go inside DICTION.
explanation.definitionFit: Dissection is the act of cutting something apart, as in anatomy, so it is a cutting up.

clue.text: Fish with line that has weights, attached to rod

definitions.text: that has weights, attached to rod
definitions.note: a descriptive definition for a thing

blocks.note: a barbel is a freshwater fish
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: An angler's fish on a weighted line attached to a fishing rod.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface puts us at the riverbank with a weighted line on a rod; the rod is really the bar of gym equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: A barbell is a long metal bar used in weightlifting, with weight discs fixed at each end.

clue.text: Put down what's concerning newspapers?

blocks.note: re means about or concerning
the press is newspapers collectively

explanation.surface: A question about suppressing the newspapers, as in censorship.
explanation.definitionFit: To repress is to put down or subdue, as a government represses a revolt.

clue.text: Organisation including all constituents in any matter

definitions.text: Organisation including all constituents in any matter

blocks.note: surface reading: a body that represents every voter, like a political party
setter's reading: the chemical elements that make up all physical matter, laid out in a chart

explanation.walkthrough: 'Organisation' and 'constituents' suggest politics; the constituents are the chemical elements and matter is physical substance.
explanation.definitionFit: The chemistry chart arranges every known element, and every substance is built from those elements.

clue.text: Changed gear, ruined car, or part of one

indicators.note: what is changed is altered, so the letters that follow are made into something different

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A mechanic's report: gears changed, car wrecked, or a component damaged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruined' looks like a second anagram signal, but it is part of the fodder; 'one' points back to the car of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The undercarriage is the underside framework of a vehicle, carrying its wheels, so it is part of a car.

clue.text: Stolen drug found in repeated check in mixture

indicators.note: something found in another thing lies inside it

blocks.note: stolen goods are hot
CH is the chess abbreviation for check, given twice
pot is cannabis

explanation.surface: Stolen narcotics discovered during a series of police checks.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotchpotch is a jumbled mixture of different things.

clue.text: Excel in fight, getting case dismissed? Just the opposite

indicators.note: the opposite order to the phrase as written, so the two parts swap places

blocks.note: a batsman who is dismissed is out
a box is a case

explanation.surface: A boxer wins a bout and then has the charges against them thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case dismissed' would give the words box and out; 'just the opposite' puts them the other way round.
explanation.definitionFit: To outbox an opponent is to beat them at boxing, outclassing them in a fight.

clue.text: Placed under powerful lamp till food gets ruined

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked out of shape, so its letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Food left under a heat lamp until it spoils.
explanation.definitionFit: Floodlit means lit by floodlights, the strong lamps used over stadiums and buildings.

clue.text: Hunting animal using rope and dart, possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals one possible arrangement among many of the given letters

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A hunter catching animals with a rope and a tranquilliser dart.
explanation.definitionFit: A predator is an animal that kills and eats others, so it hunts.

clue.text: Height gained by police aircraft

indicators.note: something gained by another is taken into it, so it ends up inside

blocks.note: coppers is slang for police officers
H is the abbreviation for height

explanation.surface: Police helicopters climbing to altitude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Police aircraft' looks like one phrase but splits: police is wordplay, aircraft alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Choppers is informal for helicopters, which are aircraft.

clue.text: Starting-points for big wins, leaders having dropped out

indicators.note: the leaders are the first letters, and dropping them out removes each word's opening letter

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Talk of where big sporting victories begin, after the frontrunners drop out of a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For' looks like a link joining definition to wordplay, but it is the first of three words to lose their initials.
explanation.definitionFit: Origins are beginnings, the points from which things start.

clue.text: Provided backing as company goes into complete failure

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the word is read from end to start

blocks.note: if means provided that
taken as written
CO is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A firm, having received financial support, collapses anyway.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiasco is a humiliating, total failure.

clue.text: Inheritance from father certainly is holding chap up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top
one thing holding another has it inside

blocks.note: sure means certainly
a chap is a man

explanation.surface: A man insists that what he got from his father is holding a fellow up.
explanation.definitionFit: Children traditionally take their father's family name, so a surname is passed down from him.

clue.text: Part of God's acre duly consecrated

indicators.note: part of a phrase means only a run of its letters is used

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word, all of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: Part of the churchyard has been properly consecrated.
explanation.walkthrough: God's acre is an old name for a churchyard, which fits the surface's consecrated ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Sacred means holy, made sacred by consecration or dedicated to God.

clue.text: Crazy rant permitted in newspaper, for example

indicators.note: something crazy is wild and disordered, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An unhinged tirade allowed into a paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Printed matter is any material produced by printing, and a newspaper is one example.

clue.text: Deflated but not flat? That can be done

indicators.note: but not means excluding, so the named word is taken out

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, the letters to remove

explanation.surface: A tyre that is deflated but not completely flat can still be fixed.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads loosely as a noun for 'a thing that is done'.
explanation.definitionFit: A deed is an act or action, something performed.

clue.text: Travel permit for one arriving originally with two others

definitions.text: one arriving originally with two others

blocks.note: a trip is a journey, or to trip is to travel
to let is to permit

explanation.surface: A travel permit issued for one person arriving with two companions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arriving originally' means being born: a triplet is one of three born together.
explanation.definitionFit: A triplet is one of three children born at the same birth, so they arrive alongside two siblings.

clue.text: Bone structure that may be broken in big race

indicators.note: something broken is smashed apart, so its letters are rebuilt in another order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Bones that might get broken during a major horse race, after a fall.
explanation.definitionFit: The ribcage is the bony frame of ribs enclosing the chest.

clue.text: Person who entertains crowd

blocks.note: first meaning: one who receives guests
second meaning: a great number

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a performer entertaining an audience; the crowd is a separate meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: A host receives and entertains guests, and a host is also a large number of people or things.

clue.text: Attacking position in game leading to point

indicators.note: one part leading to another comes first, ahead of the next

blocks.note: bridge is a card game
a head is a point, as of land

explanation.surface: A chess or board-game move that sets up an attack on a key point.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridgehead is a strong position seized in enemy territory from which an attack can be pushed forward.
